name: Michael Bridgford
bio: Michael Bridgford is an independent candidate for Iowa's 1st district who grew up on a family farm near the Quad Cities that his family homesteaded in the 1830s. He earned an MBA from Northwestern and has worked as an employee and small-business owner; Radio Iowa describes him as a Quad Cities financial advisor. The Forward Party has endorsed him.

platform.point: Supports term limits, a congressional stock-trading ban and campaign finance reform.
Backs a deficit cap near 3% of GDP with pay-as-you-go rules requiring new spending to be offset.
Would lift the payroll tax cap, protect benefits for people near retirement and slow benefit growth only for top earners.
Wants upfront price disclosure, site-neutral billing, and higher Medicare payments for rural Critical Access Hospitals.
Proposes a federal AI impact fee, local control over data center siting, and closed-loop cooling requirements.
Supports permanent year-round E15 ethanol sales, stronger antitrust enforcement in agriculture and predictable tariff policy.
Wants more EQIP conservation funding, federal cancer-cluster investigations and opposes pesticide liability shields.
Supports federal waivers that cut reporting rules and redirect money to Iowa K-12 public school classrooms.

economy.evidence: Mixes pay-as-you-go budget limits with aggressive antitrust enforcement, a lifted Social Security tax cap and a federal AI impact fee.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security benefits and fund rural hospitals, but said Medicare for All or a public option is not feasible and favors price transparency instead.

liberty.evidence: On speech, pledges to oppose federal pressure on platforms to censor legal speech; no stated positions found on abortion, drugs or guns.

immigration.evidence: Told Iowa Public Radio he opposes mass deportations while acknowledging border security concerns, seeking a middle path; a general statement.

foreign.evidence: On Iran, favors diplomacy and says Congress must authorize any escalation; a general statement.

tech.evidence: Proposes a federal AI impact fee, local veto over data center siting, automation disclosure mandates and accountability for social media algorithms affecting kids.

education.evidence: Proposes redirecting federal compliance money to Iowa K-12 public school classrooms to cut class sizes and protect electives.

notes: Detailed issue text was read from the campaign site's Issues page plus Iowa Public Radio and IVN coverage; several local outlets (KCCI, WHO 13, Iowa Capital Dispatch) blocked automated access. No stated positions were found on abortion, guns, policing or religion, and his energy stance (E15 plus voluntary conservation) was too mixed to score.

name: Rick Stewart
bio: Rick Stewart is a retired businessman from Cedar Rapids and the Libertarian candidate for Iowa's 2nd district; Radio Iowa reported in August 2026 that he had qualified for the November ballot. He previously ran for U.S. Senate as an independent in 2014, Linn County sheriff in 2016, Iowa Secretary of Agriculture in 2018, U.S. Senate as the Libertarian nominee in 2020, and governor in 2022.

platform.point: Has made ending the war on drugs his top priority, including legalizing psilocybin for therapeutic use (2022 governor race).
Said in his 2020 Senate run that all U.S. wars should end, including in Afghanistan.
Proposed capping congressional bills at five pages and requiring federal programs to be reauthorized every 10 years (2020).
Opposed federal tariffs during his 2020 Senate campaign.

economy.evidence: In 2020 he called for a simpler federal government, opposed tariffs and proposed sunsetting programs every 10 years; a general statement from a prior campaign.

welfare.evidence: In his 2020 Senate run he called for ending the 'war on poverty'; a general slogan without specific program cuts.

liberty.evidence: On drugs, calls ending prohibition his top priority and pledged in 2022 to legalize psilocybin; no stated positions found on abortion, guns or speech.

foreign.evidence: Said in 2020 that all U.S. wars should end, including the war in Afghanistan.

notes: No 2026 campaign website or platform was found; scores rely on his own statements reported by Radio Iowa in his 2020 and 2022 campaigns, and 2026 coverage (June and August) reported no positions. Stances on immigration, energy, tech, education, policing and religion remain unknown.

name: Dave Bushaw
bio: Dave Bushaw is from northeast Iowa, raised in West Union, and ran a squash farm, Solidarity Fields, from 2014 to 2019. He was a rural field organizer for Bernie Sanders' 2020 campaign, built Midwest operations for the rural group United Today, Stronger Tomorrow from 2020 to 2025, and performs as a folk and labor musician. The Forward Party has endorsed him.

platform.point: Endorses Sen. Bernie Sanders' Medicare for All plan to replace premiums, copays and deductibles.
Would end right-to-work laws, penalize anti-union employers and extend labor law protections to farm workers.
Supports the Head Start for America's Children Act to expand early learning and pre-K.
Favors expanded naturalization and a legal pathway to citizenship for undocumented workers rather than enforcement raids.
Calls for nationwide decriminalization and expungement of non-violent marijuana convictions.
Wants FTC probes of private equity landlords and a restored Glass-Steagall split of commercial and investment banking.
Opposes federal preemption of state and local regulation of data center expansion.
Supports overturning Citizens United, a national ballot referendum process and an Election Day holiday.

economy.evidence: Proposes ending right-to-work laws, FTC action against private equity in housing and reinstating Glass-Steagall.

welfare.evidence: Endorses Sen. Sanders' Medicare for All plan and a major Head Start and pre-K expansion.

liberty.evidence: On drugs, backs nationwide marijuana decriminalization and expungement; on guns, rejects confiscation and favors voluntary safety classes; no abortion position found.

immigration.evidence: Favors a legal pathway to citizenship for undocumented workers instead of enforcement raids.

foreign.evidence: Objects to military spending abroad, citing funding for Israel's Iron Dome, and prioritizes domestic defense over overseas intervention.

tech.evidence: Opposes federal preemption that would block state and local regulation of data centers and wants AI workforce displacement evaluated.

education.evidence: Supports the Head Start for America's Children Act to expand publicly funded early learning.

notes: Positions come from the campaign's Platform page plus Radio Iowa coverage. The platform does not address abortion, energy, policing, K-12 schools or religion.

name: Brendan Gomez
bio: Brendan Gomez is the Constitution Party nominee for Idaho's 1st congressional district. He was also the party's nominee for the seat in 2024, when he received about 1.5 percent of the vote.
notes: Checked Wikipedia's 2024 and 2026 Idaho House election pages, which list only his party and 2024 result; Idaho Press and Idaho Capital Sun searches were blocked and no campaign site was found. No public policy statements were found.

name: Will Johanson
bio: Will Johanson is an engineer in Idaho's semiconductor industry and a U.S. Navy veteran who served as a nuclear machinist's mate aboard the USS Georgia until 2020. He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in materials science and engineering from Boise State University. He was raised in California's Central Valley and is based in Boise.

platform.point: Pledges to vote against any budget that increases the national debt, blaming deficit spending for inflation.
Describes taxation as theft.
Holds that Second Amendment rights should not be infringed.
Supports expanded domestic drilling, fracking and critical mineral mining instead of imports.
Calls for closing the border.
Says abortion is not an issue he intends to prioritize.
Argues government overreach and red tape hurt working families and slow innovation.
Supports a strong national defense.

economy.evidence: Calls taxation theft and pledges to vote against any budget that adds to the national debt.

liberty.evidence: On guns, says Second Amendment rights shall not be infringed; on abortion he says it is not his priority; no drug or speech positions found.

immigration.evidence: States the border should be closed; a general statement without specific measures.

energy.evidence: Supports expanding U.S. drilling, fracking and critical mineral mining.

notes: Positions come from the campaign's Issues and About pages; Idaho news sites blocked automated searches. His 'strong national defense' statement was too general to score foreign policy, and welfare, tech, education, policing and religion remain unknown.

name: Carta Sierra
bio: Carta Sierra is the Constitution Party nominee for Idaho's 2nd congressional district. Sierra, described on Wikipedia as a paralegal and perennial candidate, was also the party's nominee for the seat in 2024 and received about 2.4 percent of the vote.
notes: Checked Wikipedia's 2024 and 2026 Idaho House election pages; Idaho Press and Idaho Capital Sun searches were blocked and no campaign site was found. No public policy statements were found.

name: Emre Houser
current_role: Small-business owner and Idaho National Guard member
bio: Emre Houser is an Idaho small-business owner of more than 15 years with over 27 years of military service, including the Air Force from 1995 to 1999 and the Idaho National Guard since 1999, with a 2003 deployment to Iraq. He has lived in Idaho for nearly 30 years. He was previously registered as a Democrat and became unaffiliated in 2025.

platform.point: Opposes selling Idaho's public lands or letting private fences block access to them.
Proposes automatic VA enrollment at discharge and more VA funding.
Wants Medicare and Medicaid to get VA-style negotiated drug prices, handled by CMS rather than the president.
Would remove the wage cap on Social Security payroll taxes.
Targets the tax gap, 'buy, borrow, die' loopholes and high earners who do not file returns.
Calls for breaking up concentration in meatpacking, dairy and media, and outlawing stock buybacks.
Supports term limits, a congressional stock-trading ban and overturning Citizens United.
Criticizes current tariffs as a hidden household tax and calls for more responsible tariff policy.

economy.evidence: Proposes outlawing stock buybacks, breaking up meatpacking and media monopolies, lifting the Social Security wage cap and closing 'buy, borrow, die' loopholes.

security.evidence: Criticizes the incumbent for votes allowing warrantless government access to private data, signaling opposition to warrantless surveillance.

immigration.evidence: Cites ICE raids disrupting farm workers as harmful to smaller farms; a general statement without a broader immigration plan.

tech.evidence: Proposes applying a broadcast-style fairness doctrine to social media and breaking up concentration in the media market.

notes: Positions come from the campaign's Platform and About pages; Idaho news sites blocked automated searches. His platform calls healthcare decisions private between patient and provider but does not name abortion, so liberty was left unscored, and foreign policy, energy, education and religion remain unknown.

name: Tripp Hutchinson
bio: Tripp Hutchinson is a member of the Ketchum City Council. He was born and raised in Idaho and is running as an independent for Idaho's 2nd congressional district, saying his campaign will not accept money from billionaires or corporate PACs.

platform.point: Wants Idaho families to be able to live comfortably on a single household income.
Supports a minimum tax for billionaires.
Would ban corporate purchases of single-family homes.
Supports paid family leave, funding Social Security and Medicare drug price negotiation.
Wants to end forever wars, return war powers to Congress and audit the Pentagon.
Backs right-to-repair guarantees, comprehensive data privacy law and a ban on junk fees.
Would ban foreign governments from buying American farmland.
Supports term limits, a stock-trading ban, a lifetime lobbying ban, ending gerrymandering and overturning Citizens United.

economy.evidence: Supports a billionaire minimum tax, a ban on corporate purchases of single-family homes and a ban on junk fees.

welfare.evidence: Lists paid family leave, funding Social Security and Medicare drug negotiation among his platform items.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending 'forever wars', returning war powers to Congress and auditing the Pentagon.

tech.evidence: Supports comprehensive data privacy legislation and right-to-repair guarantees for cars, machinery and electronics.

notes: Positions come from the campaign's home and Platform pages; the Idaho Mountain Express and other Idaho news sites blocked or rate-limited automated searches, so Ketchum council votes were not reviewed. Stances on abortion, guns, immigration, energy, education and religion remain unknown.
